official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'It is not possible to get a scholarship to cover the tuition fee for the first year, but the University offers an Early Bird discount of 2,000 EUR for master's degree applicants.' and 'All students who fulfill the requirements are eligible for a scholarship that covers 50% of the tuition fee for the next study year. The scholarships are awarded based on academic merits only.'
official.funding_period: one-off; 50% of tuition per academic year
benefits: Early Bird discount of 2,000 EUR for newly admitted master's degree students who accept the study offer and pay the tuition fee within 28 days after the admission decisions have been published
University of Turku Merit Scholarship covering 50% of the tuition fee for the next study year, awarded to all students who fulfil the requirements
Master's degree students: 50% of the 2nd year tuition fee
Bachelor's degree students: 50% of the 2nd and 3rd year tuition fees
eligibility: Scholarships are offered for both Bachelor's and Master's level studies, for students who are subject to tuition fees, and are based on studies completed at the University of Turku
Students who have paid for their studies during their first year(s) of studies at the University of Turku are eligible to apply for the Merit Scholarship
Tuition fees will be charged from citizens of a country outside the European Union (EU) and the European Economic Area (EEA) or Switzerland
Master's degree students: the merit scholarship covers 50% of the 2nd year tuition fee; the requirement for receiving the scholarship is 55cr during the first study year

Bachelor's degree students: the merit scholarship covers 50% of the 2nd and 3rd year tuition fees; 55cr during the first study year for the 2nd study year, and 110cr during the first and second study year for the 3rd study year
The Early Bird discount is not available for applicants of the bachelor's degree programmes
requirements: Credit requirement: 55cr during the first study year (master's, for the 2nd study year); 55cr during the first study year and 110cr during the first and second study year (bachelor's, for the 3rd study year)
Grade requirement: an average score of 3.0 or higher on a grading scale of 1-5

Finnish requirement: at least 4 credits of Finnish completed before applying for the scholarship for the first time; these credits can be part of the 55 credit requirement, and other previous Finnish studies or proven Finnish proficiency are assessed case by case
A separate merit scholarship application is required: admission services invite all eligible applicants to apply when the application round opens in spring
Early Bird discount: the applicant must accept the study offer and pay the tuition fee within 28 days after the admission decisions have been published
documents: Scanned original degree certificate in the original language plus an official English, Finnish or Swedish translation, attached to the online application form (nothing is sent by post or email)
Official transcript of records covering the full length of studies with grades, credits, completion times and the grading scale used, plus an official translation
Proof of English language skills, attached by the end of the supplementation period (28 January 2027)
A scan or photo of the passport information page or national ID card (both sides of a Finnish residence permit card, if held)
Programme-specific documents where the admission criteria require them, such as motivation letters
selection_criteria: The scholarships are awarded based on academic merits only
Credits completed at the University of Turku in the first study year(s): 55cr, or 110cr for bachelor's year three
Average score of 3.0 or higher on the 1-5 grading scale
At least 4 credits of Finnish completed before the first scholarship application
All students who fulfil these requirements will be awarded a scholarship for the following academic year
coverage: Merit Scholarship: 50% of the tuition fee for the next study year
Master's degree students: 50% of the 2nd year tuition fee
Bachelor's degree students: 50% of the 2nd and 3rd year tuition fees
Early Bird discount: 2,000 EUR for newly admitted master's degree students
No coverage of living costs, travel or installation - students must support themselves independently
application_method: Degree admission: apply through the Studyinfo.fi online portal during the January application period only (7-21 January 2027 for the next intake); up to six programmes in the joint application, maximum three at the University of Turku
Early Bird discount: no separate application - accept the study offer and pay the tuition fee within 28 days after the admission decisions have been published
Merit Scholarship: separate application, submitted only after admission services invite all eligible applicants when the application round opens in spring
official.application_route: Admission via Studyinfo.fi in January (next round 7-21 January 2027, 100 EUR application fee for applicants from outside the EU/EEA); the Early Bird discount is granted automatically on timely acceptance and payment; the Merit Scholarship is applied for only when invited by admission services in spring
official.citizenship_residency: Tuition fees are charged from citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, and the scholarships are for students subject to those fees. Fees are not charged from holders of an EU Blue Card in Finland, a permanent residence permit in Finland, a continuous residence permit granted for purposes other than studies, a long-term resident's EU residence permit issued in Finland, an EU Family Member's Residence Card in Finland, or temporary protection status; a fixed-term continuous (A) permit must be valid at the start of each academic year (1 August) and granted on grounds other than studies. Students in degree programmes taught in Finnish, exchange students and doctoral students are never charged.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists precisely for fee-liable non-Eu/EEA and non-Swiss international students; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay no tuition and are therefore outside the scheme
official.duration: The Merit Scholarship covers the following academic year: master's year two, or bachelor's years two and three
official.description: The University of Turku charges tuition fees from non-EU/EEA citizens and supports merited, motivated students with scholarships: a 2,000 EUR Early Bird discount for newly admitted master's students who accept their study offer and pay tuition within 28 days of the admission decisions, and the University of Turku Merit Scholarship covering 50% of tuition for the following academic year(s), awarded on academic merit alone to every student who meets the credit, grade and Finnish-language requirements.
official.program_type: Tuition-fee scholarship for admitted non-EU/EEA degree students: a first-year Early Bird discount (master's only) plus a merit-based 50% tuition scholarship for later study years
official.english_requirement: The scholarship itself publishes no English requirement; the degree admission rules require documented excellent English skills: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with 6.0 or more in each subtest, TOEFL iBT overall 92 with writing 22 (tests taken before 21 January 2026) or overall 4.5 with 4.0 in each subtest (tests taken on or after 21 January 2026), PTE Academic overall 68 with writing 61, Cambridge C2 Proficiency or C1 Advanced with pass grade A, B or C, or YKI with a minimum score of 5 in all subtests; exemptions apply for higher-education degrees or secondary education completed in English in listed countries. Proof must be attached by the application deadline and cannot be added conditionally after admission.

verification.notes: All figures taken directly from utu.fi pages fetched on 10 October 2026. The Merit Scholarship is published as a percentage of tuition (programme fees range from EUR 1,500 to EUR 12,000 per academic year), so the only fixed published cash figure is the EUR 2,000 Early Bird discount; the 50% value is recorded in the coverage fields rather than as a single amount.

applicant_utility.summary: Turku pays only after you have already paid: year one must be funded entirely from your own pocket, and the reward arrives in year two (bachelor's: years two and three) as a 50% tuition cut, with a EUR 2,000 one-off Early Bird discount available only to master's entrants who accept and pay within 28 days of the admission decisions. The Merit Scholarship is guaranteed rather than competitive - every student who clears the credit, grade and Finnish requirements receives it - so the real test is whether you can hit 55-110 UTU credits, a 3.0/5 average and 4 Finnish credits while studying in a second language. Neither scheme touches living costs, so budget tuition plus roughly EUR 700-900 a month out of pocket.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-liable non-EU/EEA students who can self-fund the first year, want a guaranteed rather than luck-based tuition cut from year two, and are willing to learn Finnish from day one.
application_readiness_checklist: Book your English test months ahead: the result must be attached by 28 January 2027 and stay verifiable until at least 21 February 2027 (TOEFL and PTE lapse after two years, IELTS after three).

Order original-language degree certificates and transcripts plus official translations now; for electronically issued documents make sure your institution issues a verifiable e-transcript or an electronically signed copy.

Stage the full first-year cost before you accept anything: tuition (programme fees run EUR 1,500-12,000 per academic year) plus the EUR 9,600 bank balance Migri expects for a student residence permit for studies of a year or more.
Diarise the day admission decisions are published - the 28-day Early Bird clock starts then, not when you get around to reading the email.
Enrol in Finnish for Foreigners in your first semester and bank at least 4 credits before the spring scholarship application window opens.
Check whether you are actually exempt from tuition (EU Blue Card in Finland, A permit on non-study grounds, temporary protection) - if you are exempt you fall outside this scheme entirely.
common_rejection_risks: Falling short on credits: 55 ECTS in a single first year is close to a full-time load, so a light course selection, a deferred exam or a retake can put the 50% cut out of reach - and only credits completed at UTU count.
The average drifting below 3.0 on the 1-5 scale even though the credit count is met.
Losing the Early Bird discount by missing the 28-day acceptance and payment window after the admission decisions are published.
Arriving assuming a first-year scholarship exists - the university states plainly that no first-year tuition scholarship is possible.
Sitting the wrong English test, combining scores from different test dates, or letting a result pass its verifiability window before 21 February 2027.
Bachelor's applicants expecting the Early Bird discount, which is explicitly not available to them.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The whole first year, plus half of tuition in every covered year: full first-year tuition (EUR 1,500-12,000 depending on programme, most EUR 10,000-12,000), living costs the university puts at EUR 600-900 per month with a EUR 800/month minimum, student union membership of about EUR 54-55 per academic year, Kela student healthcare fee of EUR 35.35 per term in 2026, an electronic first residence permit application fee of EUR 450, housing deposits of EUR 250-500 and furnishing costs for an unfurnished flat, plus a laptop and course materials.
document_audit: Certified true copies are accepted only if issued by the awarding institution or Finland's Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) - a local notary stamp does not count.
Screenshots from your university's study portal are not accepted as electronic transcripts unless the document carries a verification code, link or official electronic signature.
You cannot edit any application answers after 21 January, and all attachments must be uploaded by 28 January 2027, 3:00 p.m. Finnish time.
Name University of Turku as a test-score recipient where possible (TOEFL code 9701; SAT results to institutional code 7838 for bachelor's group I applicants).
No scholarship-specific document list is published: the merit scholarship application runs on your university records plus whatever the spring invitation email asks for.
alerts: The scholarship page states its information is for students admitted in 2026 and was last updated 10 March 2026 (correcting the Early Bird window from 30 to 28 days) - re-check the page before relying on 2026 dates or figures for a 2027 intake.
The Early Bird clock runs from publication of the admission decisions, not from your own reply - a holiday or slow bank transfer can cost EUR 2,000.
Finnish is a hard gate: 4 credits before your first scholarship application, and those credits can be counted inside the 55-credit requirement, so take Finnish early rather than late.
Only one study place leading to a higher-education degree in Finland may be accepted per academic term.
Finnish state student financial aid generally requires permanent residence granted on grounds other than study, so do not build a budget around Kela.
The separate Fulbright-University of Turku Graduate Award (EUR 1,000/month plus tuition, US citizens only) is a different scheme from this scholarship and discount.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the Studyinfo.fi joint application in January with every enclosure uploaded by 28 January; on an offer, accept and pay the tuition fee within 28 days to trigger the Early Bird; then wait for the spring email from admission services inviting you into the separate Merit Scholarship application.
